<Doc1>
Screening Test/Interview Questions for Copywriter (Remote) Position

Candidate’s Name: Dylan O'Connor

1. Are you currently employed? 
A: I am not currently employed.

2. Describe what copywriter means to you.
A: A copywriter is a strategic communicator and storyteller who collaborates to develop a brand's unique voice and craft branded messaging. A copywriter identifies, researches, and understands the brand's target audience, and uses this understanding to create persuasive, engaging content. A copywriter can adapt their tone and messaging to fit various formats and goals, making sure their work resonates across different mediums.

3. Tell me about a time when you turned an unhappy customer into a delighted customer.
A: My role as Product Research Manager at an Amazon FBA required me to be dynamic and occasionally included handling customer complaints. In one instance, a customer left a negative review on our seller account after receiving a defective item that he needed to use expeditiously. The customer reached out to us on Amazon’s messaging system detailing the problem and I promptly responded to offer him a solution. I assured him that I would personally set up a replacement order with expedited shipping to meet the needs for his timeline. I kept the customer updated and followed up once the order was set to arrive. The customer informed me that the new unit arrived and worked properly, and that he would update his review to reflect the service he received.

4. How important do you think it is to work collaboratively with other Copywriters and teams across a company? 
A: Collaborating with other copywriters and teams across a company is an essential part of any copywriting project. Working with other copywriters and teams allows ideas to be shared, work to be refined, and the brand’s voice and messaging to remain consistent and unified across different works and platforms.



5. How well do you work under high pressure/in high-stress situations?
A: I work well under high pressure/high stress situations because I strive to maintain a calm, solution-oriented mindset. When faced with an issue I am unsure how to solve, I take a step back, break it into manageable parts, and focus on what I can do to improve the situation rather than panicking over the problem.

6. What do you do when you don’t know how to help a customer? 
A: When I don't know how to help a customer, I remain calm, transparent, and ask for their patience while I look into a solution. I review any resources or materials I have access to and if I still cannot find a solution, I consult with another member of the team who may be more knowledgeable on the issue. Once I have the solution, I get back to the customer as quickly as I can, thank them for their patience, and follow up to make sure their issue has been fully resolved.

7. Do you consider yourself a ‘people person’? Why or why not?
A: Yes, I consider myself a people person, and it is one of my strengths as a collaborator and communicator. In my previous role at an e-commerce startup, being a people person was essential. My duties varied on a day-to-day basis, and I often needed to communicate with suppliers, support, customers, and work directly with the other members of my team. I genuinely enjoy collaborating with others toward a shared goal, which is one of the reasons I love copywriting.

8. What Copywriter tools do you have experience with? 
A: I am proficient with Microsoft Office, Google Suite, and Canva, which are tools I have used for copywriting in previous work. I have also used AI writing tools like Grammarly to assist me while writing. Additionally, I have experience using Trello and Slack for team collaboration.

9. What would you do if a frustrated customer complained about a widely known problem with the company’s service? 
A: If a frustrated customer complained about a widely known problem with the company’s service, I would offer transparency and any possible resolution. I would acknowledge their frustration, reassure them that the company is aware of the issue, and explain that steps are being taken to address it. If a temporary solution existed, I would offer it to help mitigate the problem. Finally, I would thank the customer for their patience and understanding while the company works on a permanent solution.

10. What tactics do you use to calm upset customer? 
A: When working with an upset customer, I make sure to stay calm and focus on de-escalation. I first let the customer know I hear and understand their problem, so they know they are being listened to. I apologize for any inconvenience that has been caused, then calmly offer solutions or alternatives to resolve the customer’s issues or concerns. Throughout the conversation, I make sure to actively listen to the customer’s concerns and maintain a solution-oriented mindset. I always make sure to apologize again and thank the customer for their patience at the end of the conversation.

11. Tell me about your experience working remotely. 
A: In my previous role, I operated in a hybrid position, where about 80% of my work was remote and 20% was in-person. I have always enjoyed working remotely, and I had all of the tools available to make sure I succeeded in a remote environment, such as good internet connection, a quiet and organized workspace, and a computer with dual monitors sufficient for the work I was doing. This experience has taught me how to collaborate with colleagues remotely and I have no doubt I will excel in a fully remote position.

12. How do you stay updated on the current industry trends as well as customer expectations? 
A: I am a member of multiple online servers and forums where new resources, trends, and developments are uploaded and shared on a daily basis. Blogs, articles, copy examples, trends, and more are shared and compiled every day on these sites, and it is a great resource for staying up to date. To stay updated on customer expectations I always make sure to read incoming customer reviews to find what areas are strengths and what areas need improvement.

13. Describe your daily routine as a Copywriter. 
A: My daily routine as a copywriter consists of prioritizing tasks based on deadlines, researching, brainstorming, writing, editing, and collaborating with others. To start the day, I determine which tasks need to be prioritized based on project deadlines. Then, I research the project I’m working on, including its target audience, goals, and any necessary background information. After that, I brainstorm ideas, outline a plan, and begin writing, followed by editing and revising. Throughout the process, I collaborate with relevant team members to discuss ideas, review edits, and ensure that our work is consistent and unified. This was the general process I used recently while working with a commercial food photography business to write a food styling PDF guide. On days when I’m not working directly on projects, I dedicate time to researching new copywriting communities online, exploring shared resources, and taking online courses to improve my skills.


14. Why should we choose you over other candidates?
A: You should choose me because I bring a unique combination of skills and experience that align perfectly with the demands of this role. While I may not have years of formal copywriting experience, I have demonstrated my ability to research, write, and create compelling materials, such as the works I have included in my portfolio. In addition, my experience as a Product Research Manager has equipped me with a strong foundation in understanding target audiences, analyzing market trends, and creating content strategies that resonate. I have proven success in identifying customer needs, optimizing messaging for impact, and ensuring that every project I undertake meets its objectives. I'm also highly self-motivated, adaptable, and committed to continuous learning. I’ve recently invested time in sharpening my skills with copywriting resources and familiarizing myself with relevant tools and SEO strategies. You’ll find that my dedication, creative problem-solving, and drive to deliver results and learn make me a standout candidate for this position. DYLAN
